adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — In `updateEvent`, the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it always returns undefined and `selectedCalendar` falls back to 'primary' instead of the destination calendar's externalId; same defect in `deleteEvent` (~line 317)

adjudication.rationale:
The diff changes `destinationCalendar` to an array, but in `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent` the fallback calendar selection is implemented as:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the only time the fallback branch runs), the `.find(...)` compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, so it will almost always return `undefined`. That means `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` and downstream code will use the default/`primary` calendar instead of any destination calendar externalId. The same broken pattern appears in `deleteEvent` for `calendarId`.

This is a concrete logic defect introduced in the diff; the fallback cannot select a real destination calendar when `externalCalendarId` is missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:363 — In `createAllCalendarEvents`, the same `event` is passed to every credential's `createEvent`, so Google sets the organizer email from `destinationCalendar[0].externalId` (main host) for secondary hosts' calendars, producing wrong organizer emails; also the else-branch `createEvent(c, event)` omits `externalId`, leaving `externalCalendarId: undefined` on the reference

adjudication.rationale:
Real issue in the diff. In `createAllCalendarEvents` (packages/core/EventManager.ts), the loop calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` only when `destination.credentialId` is present, but in the `else` branch it calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing any `externalId`. Since `CalendarManager.createEvent` now returns `externalId` from that argument and `EventManager` later stores `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`, those references will end up with `externalCalendarId: undefined` for that branch.

Also, Google’s `createEvent` now derives `mainHostDestinationCalendar` from `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar[0]` and uses it to set the organizer attendee email. Because `createAllCalendarEvents` passes the same `event` object (same `destinationCalendar` array) to each credential, that organizer email logic will always use the first destination calendar’s externalId, even when inserting into a different destination calendar/credential, which can produce incorrect organizer emails for non-first calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:365 — Credentials fetched from the DB for other team members are used without checking `invalid` or that the credential's user is a host on the event type; a stale `destinationCalendar.credentialId` could write bookings into another user's calendar

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents (around the new loop over event.destinationCalendar), if a destination has credentialId but it is not found in this.calendarCredentials, the code now fetches prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } }) and uses it to call createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId). There is no verification that the fetched credential belongs to an allowed user/host for the event, nor any guard against credentialFromDB.invalid before using it. This means a stale or incorrect destinationCalendar.credentialId can cause the system to create calendar events using an arbitrary credential record not originally associated with the EventManager’s allowed credentials, which could write to the wrong user’s calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147 — `selectedCalendar` now matches on `cal.credentialId === credentialId`; older bookings or destination calendars without a `credentialId` find no match and events are created in 'primary' instead of the chosen destination calendar (regression from externalId-based matching)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In GoogleCalendarService.createEvent, the calendarId is now chosen via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and falls back to `"primary"` when no match is found. But elsewhere in the diff (EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents), there is an explicit branch for destinations *without* `destination.credentialId` where events are still created for credentials matching `destination.integration` (`createEvent(c, event)`), meaning the destinationCalendar entries in `event.destinationCalendar` can legitimately lack `credentialId`. In that case, GoogleCalendarService will not find a matching destination calendar and will create the event in the user's primary calendar instead of the intended destination externalId—this is a concrete behavior change/regression from the prior externalId-based selection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:342 — `createAllCalendarEvents` and `updateAllCalendarEvents` perform sequential awaits per destination calendar/reference with a possible DB `findUnique` each, causing N sequential DB round-trips plus calendar API calls in the request path for N hosts

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts, createAllCalendarEvents was changed to iterate `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and inside the loop it does `await prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` (when credential not already in `this.calendarCredentials`) and then `await createEvent(...)`, making those DB lookups + calendar API calls run sequentially per destination. Similarly, updateAllCalendarEvents now iterates `for (const reference of calendarReference)` and can `await prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` inside the loop, creating sequential DB round-trips per reference. This matches the finding’s claim of N sequential DB calls (and in createAllCalendarEvents, sequential calendar API calls) in the request path for N destinations/hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:604 — The catch block returns `[]` when `calendarReference` is undefined (e.g., error before references were computed), whereas it previously returned one failed result; callers expecting an error result now see silent success

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts, the catch block was changed from always returning a single failed EventResult (even when calendarReference was undefined, via `calendarReference?.type || "calendar"`) to returning `calendarReference?.map(...) ?? []`. Since `calendarReference` is initialized as `undefined` and only set later inside the try, any error thrown before references are computed will now cause the function to return an empty array, which is indistinguishable from “no calendar updates needed” for many callers. This is a behavior regression relative to the previous code and can mask failures.
